BREAKING — Laredo ISD police arrested Mitchelle Cardenas on Tuesday morning, October 20, 2026, on a felony charge of possessing a controlled substance in a drug-free zone, according to Webb County booking records.

Cardenas was arrested at 10:39 a.m. and booked into the Webb County Jail on one count of possession of a controlled substance, Penalty Group 2, less than 1 gram, in a drug-free zone (charge code POSS CS PG2<1G DFZ IAT) — a third-degree felony under Texas law. A judge set bond at $10,000. The case stems from an alleged offense dated October 9, 2026, and was executed on a warrant by the Laredo Independent School District Police Department.

The drug-free-zone allegation matters: Texas law designates areas in and around schools, youth centers, and similar places as drug-free zones, and a drug offense committed inside one carries enhanced punishment. Penalty Group 2 covers substances such as MDMA, methamphetamine in certain forms, and other controlled drugs. A third-degree felony in Texas is punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000.

The arrest was carried out by a school district police department on an offense alleged to have occurred earlier this month. Webb Watch 956 will follow this case as it moves through the Webb County courts — whether the charge holds, is reduced, or is dismissed is now a matter for the court record.

An arrest is an allegation, not a conviction. Mitchelle Cardenas is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Sources: Webb County Sheriff's Office Booking Jail Search (Oct. 20, 2026); Webb County public-access court records, Tyler Odyssey portal.
